_status: staged — structurally checked, NOT yet imported
_note: Grok round 8 — EU candidates and potential candidates (Montenegro, North Macedonia, Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Turkey, Ukraine, Moldova, Kosovo), plus two deliberate negative-result tests (Georgia — candidate too recent to show alignment language yet; San Marino — no EU relationship, clean not_found, contrasted against Liechtenstein). CONFIRMS Serbia's round-6 finding generalises across the whole belt: every candidate/potential-candidate uses aspirational alignment language ('in accordance with', 'compatible with', 'following'), never a member state's binding 'shall/must' — and this holds regardless of how long the country has been a candidate (Turkey: 1999, still voluntary). relationship_type left as methodology_depends_on pending review of whether the whole candidate set should be recategorised as cites, matching Serbia; flagged here rather than decided unilaterally per country.

_dropped.why: MONSTAT's own quoted text cites "Regulation (EU) No 1306/2010" as the source of ESA 2010 Annex A. That regulation number does not match ESA 2010 (Regulation (EU) No 549/2013) and does not correspond to any known EU regulation on national accounts. Quoted verbatim as found rather than silently corrected, per Research.1.md §2 — but NOT verified against the primary MONSTAT document directly, only against Grok's transcription. Needs a direct check of the source PDF before this edge is treated as fully confirmed: either MONSTAT's own document contains the error, or it was introduced in transcription.

Georgia, EU candidate only since late 2023. Geostat's own national accounts documentation states SNA 2008 as its basis; ESA 2010 appears only indirectly via Eurostat recommendations for revisions (HERP) and the Code of Practice, with no explicit alignment-obligation language. A clean, informative negative result — the newest candidacy has not yet produced published ESA 2010 alignment language, consistent with the pattern taking time to show up in public documentation.

_dropped.edge: sm-statistics-office -> esa-2010 or any comparable framework
_dropped.why: San Marino: no EU membership, no candidate status, included deliberately as a dead-end test (contrast to Liechtenstein, which turned out to have distinct ESA-aligned accounts despite similar size). Searches for a San Marino statistics office, national accounts, ESA/SEC 2010 returned only pre-2010 IMF GDDS references to ESA 95, an IMF note on the general inadequacy of San Marino's national accounts statistics, and a 2026 news item describing a newly created Unità Nazionale di Statistica aimed at future international alignment. No current published national-accounts series exists. The absence is real and, per the 2026 item, provisional rather than permanent — San Marino appears to be a country mid-transition toward having a statistics office at all.

_dropped.edge: EU-side document (e.g. the Statistical Requirements Compendium) naming a specific candidate country by name
_dropped.why: Checked directly this round. The SRC states its purpose as monitoring "the enlargement countries (candidate countries and potential candidates)" as a group; no instance was found of the SRC's own text, or any other EU-side document, naming a specific candidate country's obligations individually. Every confirmed cross-layer edge in this branch to date runs from the national office's own words toward the EU instrument — none run the other way, including for candidates. This is the eighth round to test that direction and the eighth to come back empty.
